title: Review of c06's somatic decline: on fresh seed 5, dying cells fall from yield rank 0.39 / 0.28 at birth to 0.02 at death (claim / low mutation), marker flat
summary: Ran c06's birthfate.py on two fresh seed-5 genealogies: my T=100000 genealogy of the claim world (mutation 0.02 x 0.05; 20261025T0935-c07-review-pcell-contained) and a new T=100000 genealogy of this finding's low-mutation world (0.002 x 0.1) made with c06's genealogy.py, plus a labkit pack of the low-mutation world. Claim rate: dying cells' yield rank birth / mid-life / death 0.39 / 0.20 / 0.02 (31 cells; marker 0.52 / 0.65 / 0.69); death share low-born 0.63 vs high-born 0.33 (marker 0.38 vs 0.53). Low mutation: 0.28 / 0.10 / 0.02 (7 dying cells; marker 0.68 / 0.58 / 0.57); death share low-born 0.38 vs high-born 0.08 (marker 0.11 vs 0.28); parent-daughter yield r 0.86, 17 persistent splits, 19 deaths. The particles sheet shows cells shifting colour over their lives. The finding replicates: most of the death bias is a within-life decline; birth rank also predicts death on this seed.

observations.H: data/birthfate_claimmu_s5.txt: dying cells rank 0.39 -> 0.20 -> 0.02 (marker 0.52 -> 0.69); data/birthfate_lowmu_s5.txt: 0.28 -> 0.10 -> 0.02 (marker 0.68 -> 0.57); rerun/seed5/particles.png: cells change colour during their lives

controls_run.H: inert marker zm in the same genealogies (data/birthfate_*_s5.txt)

verdicts.limitation: Small counts in the low-mutation run (7 mature dying cells). On this seed birth rank does predict death at both rates (0.63 vs 0.33, 0.38 vs 0.08), more than on c06's seed 0, so 'kind at birth predicts death only weakly' is seed-dependent; the within-life decline is the robust part. The marker is not uniform (it drifts upward among dying cells).
